name: Marcus's cocoa mug
description: Marcus's fireside mug, still on the side table. A faint greenish residue clings to the inside rim. The mug is still faintly damp — suggesting the cocoa was warm a few hours ago.

name: Empty digitalis extract vial
description: A small glass vial, unlabelled, found in the ash of Ruth's cottage fireplace the morning after — the glass is heat-cracked but intact enough to confirm a plant-based glycoside residue. Consistent with foxglove extract.

name: Foxglove stand in Ruth's garden
description: A substantial stand of foxglove (digitalis purpurea) in Ruth's garden, partly harvested. Several stems show fresh cut marks at the base, as if material was removed recently.

name: Ruth's original birth certificate
description: Found folded inside the binding of a book in Marcus's study: Ruth Margaret Bell, born 1973, father: Henry Bell — the same father as Marcus Bell. The mother is listed as Doris Calder. Ruth is Marcus's illegitimate half-sister, never acknowledged.

name: Marcus's revised will — draft
description: In the study: a draft of Marcus's revised will, removing Isabella and the clinic as beneficiaries and directing the estate to 'Thomas Bell, nephew.' Crucially, a handwritten note at the bottom in Marcus's hand: 'To be finalised Thursday — but if R. contests, she may have legal standing.' Marcus knew.

name: Burnt document in Marcus's fireplace
description: Recent ash in Marcus's study fireplace — burnt last night. The surviving fragment of charred paper shows the letters '...Calder...' and '...Bell, 19...' — consistent with a birth record.

name: Elias's memory — 'Bell girl'
description: Not a physical object — an interview clue. Elias, if asked carefully, recalls that there was a Bell girl in the village decades ago — born of Henry Bell and a woman who lived on the south lane. The child was raised elsewhere. He thinks her name was Ruth.

name: Marcus's spare key — in Ruth's possession
description: Ruth has a spare key to Marcus's house, given for registered post delivery. It is the only non-family key. Ruth does not mention having it.
